:::{#def-condition-number}
#### Condition number of a positive definite matrix

Let $\matr{S}$ be a $p \times p$ [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite) matrix
with [eigenvalues](linear-algebra.qmd#def-eigenvalue)
$\eigval_{\min} \le \cdots \le \eigval_{\max}$,
all positive by [definiteness and eigenvalues](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-definite-eigenvalues).
The **condition number** of $\matr{S}$ is

$$
\condnum(\matr{S}) \eqdef \frac{\eigval_{\max}}{\eigval_{\min}}.
$$

It satisfies $\condnum(\matr{S}) \ge 1$,
with equality exactly when all eigenvalues are equal.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-condition-number}
#### A condition number of 3

$\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 }$ has eigenvalues $3$ and $1$
([eigenvalue example](linear-algebra.qmd#exm-eigenvalue)),
so $\condnum(\matr{S}) = 3 / 1 = 3$.
The identity matrix $\matr{I}_2$ has eigenvalues $1$ and $1$, so $\condnum(\matr{I}_2) = 1$.

:::
